correctness.rationale: For each t>0 the positive symmetric Neumann kernel makes the L1 error of a step exactly twice the heat crossing integral. Its derivative in the jump location equals -4 times the integral of the wrapped Gaussian spatial derivative at twice the jump location. Jacobi triple-product factors make that derivative strictly negative before the midpoint. This proves unique centered extremality. A distributional BV signed-jump decomposition gives the global bound and equality classification; Fourier cosine integration proves the odd-mode formula and Poisson summation proves the asymptotics. The standalone numerical checker executed successfully but is not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact coefficient is a natural worst-case L1 error budget for a canonical reflecting diffusion regularizer on discontinuous BV data. Its unique norming jump, strict time concavity and explicit Gaussian-to-equilibrium interpolation are nontrivial structural facts not implied by standard variation diminution or heat-kernel bounds. They matter for choosing diffusion time without an unspecified approximation constant, and are not a purely cosmetic reparameterization.
